definition_zh: 监督；指导；（对行业或机构的）监管；监考
definition_en: the act of watching over work or people and being responsible for them
core_image: 一盏悬在工序上方的灯，把每一道动作照在同一片光里
scene: 新药上市前，每一批记录都要经过同一个人签字，签字人要对记录里的每个数字负责。Good supervision catches mistakes while they are still small.
sceneCN: 这里 supervision 指对工作过程持续的查看与担责（第 1 个义项：对他人工作的监督）；句意：好的监督能在错误还小的时候就发现它。图中可辨识物件：批记录、签字栏、批号标签、台灯。

forms.label: 复数（指多种监督安排，罕用）

senses.title: Watching over other people's work
senses.definition: the act of watching other people work and being answerable for what they do
senses.definitionCN: 看住别人做事，并对他们所做之事承担责任
senses.example: Supervision of the night shift is shared between two nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班的监督由两名护士分担。
senses.why: The noun is built on supervise, so it names the state of an eye being kept above the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 supervise 构成，命名的是「有一只眼留在工作上方」的状态。

senses.title: The state of being watched over
senses.definition: the condition of having one's work checked by someone with authority
senses.definitionCN: 工作被有权限的人核查的状态
senses.example: Trainees may not handle the solvent without supervision.
senses.exampleCN: 实习生不得在无人监督的情况下接触这种溶剂。
senses.why: The same noun can shift from the watcher's side to the watched side, because both share one situation.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词可以从看的人这一边转到被看的那一边，因为两边共处同一情形。

senses.title: Guidance of a research student
senses.definition: the regular advising and checking of a student's long research project
senses.definitionCN: 对一名学生长期研究项目的定期指导与核查
senses.example: Her supervision included a short meeting every second week.
senses.exampleCN: 她的指导包括每两周一次短会。
senses.why: Research unfolds over months, so this supervision is a rhythm of meetings rather than a single inspection.
senses.whyCN: 研究要展开数月，因此这种指导是一串定期会面，而不是一次检查。

senses.title: Official regulation of an industry
senses.titleCN: 对行业或机构的官方监管
senses.definition: the control exercised by an authority over an industry or institution
senses.definitionCN: 主管机关对某个行业或机构施加的控制
senses.example: Banking supervision tightened after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后，银行业监管收紧了。
senses.why: When the eye belongs to the state rather than to an employer, watching becomes rule-making.
senses.whyCN: 当这只眼属于国家而不是雇主，看管就变成了制定规则。

senses.title: Invigilation of an examination
senses.definition: the watching of candidates during an examination
senses.definitionCN: 考试期间对考生的看管
senses.example: Supervision of the hall was handed to two outside teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 考场的监考交给了两位外校老师。
senses.why: A closed room with fixed rules is the simplest place to put one eye in charge.
senses.whyCN: 一个有固定规则的封闭房间，是安置一只眼最单纯的地方。

senses.title: Clinical supervision of practitioners
senses.definition: the regular review of a counsellor's or social worker's cases by a senior colleague
senses.definitionCN: 资深同行对咨询师或社工个案的定期复盘
senses.example: Clinical supervision is built into every counsellor's timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 临床督导被排进每位咨询师的日程。
senses.why: Here the watched person is also a professional, so the eye advises rather than polices.
senses.whyCN: 这里被看的人本身也是专业人士，因此这只眼是在建议，而不是在纠察。

senses.title: Checking of an installation or site
senses.definition: the checking of building or installation work against plans and safety rules
senses.definitionCN: 对照图纸与安全规定核查施工或安装工作
senses.example: Supervision of the gas connection took three separate visits.
senses.exampleCN: 燃气接管的监督分三次上门完成。
senses.why: Where work is fixed into a building, the eye must come back more than once.
senses.whyCN: 当工作被固定进一栋建筑，这只眼就必须不止来一次。

senses.title: Watching over children or dependants
senses.titleCN: 对儿童或无自理能力者的看护
senses.definition: the keeping of a dependent person under someone's watchful care
senses.definitionCN: 把受抚养者置于某人看护之下的状态
senses.example: The children played in the yard under their grandmother's supervision.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在祖母的看护下在院子里玩。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is simply seeing, and here seeing is extended into care.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最古老的意思只是「看见」，这里看见被延伸成了照料。

intro.en: Supervision is the noun of supervise, from Medieval Latin supervidere 'to look over'. The word has moved from a single act of inspection to a standing arrangement in offices and industries.
intro.cn: supervision 是 supervise 的名词，源自中世纪拉丁 supervidere「巡视」。这个词从一次性的检查动作，发展为机构和行业里常设的安排。

items.en: Videre 'to see' gives the vis- of supervision; its perfect stem visus also gives vision and visible.
items.cn: videre「看见」给出 supervision 里的 vis-；其完成时词干 visus 也给出 vision 与 visible。

items.en: Super 'above' fixes the direction of the gaze: the watcher stands higher than the work.
items.cn: super「在上」固定了目光的方向：看的人站在比工作更高的位置。

items.en: The participle supervisus, from supervidere, is the form English took over for both the verb and the noun.
items.cn: 由 supervidere 来的分词 supervisus，就是英语借去构成动词与名词的形式。

items.en: The Latin action ending -io, -ionis, through French -ion, turns the act of watching into the name of the arrangement, supervision.
items.cn: 拉丁语的动作名词词尾经法语进入英语，把「看」这个动作变成这套安排的名称 supervision。

items.en: Supervision appears in English in the fifteenth century alongside supervise, at first for inspection of work; the date is approximate.
items.cn: supervision 与 supervise 同在十五世纪出现于英语，最初指对工作的检查；年代为约数。

items.en: Clinical, banking and building supervision are nineteenth- and twentieth-century professional arrangements rather than new senses of the root.
items.cn: 临床、银行与工程的监督是十九、二十世纪的专业安排，而不是词根新增的含义。

note.en: The first group shares the supervise root or a near shape; the second group names neighbouring systems of watching.
note.cn: 第一组共享 supervise 词根或形音相近；第二组是相邻的看管制度。

entries.definition: The verb, naming the act rather than the standing arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指动作而不是常设安排。

entries.definition: The person who holds the watching role.
entries.definitionCN: 担任看管角色的那个人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing that role or its powers.
entries.definitionCN: 描述该角色或其权力的形容词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb, but it looks over land or a sample of people, not staff at work.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个拉丁动词，但巡视的是土地或一批受访者，不是上班的员工。

entries.definition: The English-rooted twin; it also carries the opposite sense of a missed detail.
entries.definitionCN: 英语本族的对应词，同时带有「漏看」这层相反的意思。

entries.definition: Continuous measurement, often by instruments, without necessarily commanding anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 持续测量，常靠仪表，未必对人有指挥权。

entries.definition: The rules an authority imposes, rather than the watching that enforces them.
entries.definitionCN: 主管机关施加的规则，而不是执行规则的看管。

entries.definition: Advice offered to someone learning; it lacks the authority to check.
entries.definitionCN: 给学习者提供的建议，缺少核查的权力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real suffix and the real professional phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁构件、真实的后缀与真实的专业说法。

normal.en: Super is over, visio is seeing, so supervision is the state of being seen over.
normal.cn: super 是在上，visio 是看见，supervision 就是被从上面看着的状态。

normal.en: The family runs supervise, supervisor, supervisory and supervision.
normal.cn: 同族词有 supervise、supervisor、supervisory 与 supervisorship。

normal.en: Professional phrases mark it: clinical supervision, close supervision, under supervision.
normal.cn: 专业说法标出它的用法：临床督导、严密监督、在监督之下。

normal.en: The action ending -ion turns the act of watching into an arrangement.
normal.cn: 这个动作名词词尾把「看」的动作变成一种安排。

normal.en: Where an authority does the watching, supervision becomes regulation.
normal.cn: 当看管者换成主管机关，监督就变成监管。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lights every bench at once, so no corner is dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯同时照亮每张工作台，没有角落是暗的。

abstract.en: Picture a signature line that cannot be skipped, no matter how late it is.
abstract.cn: 想象一道不能跳过的签字栏，无论多晚。

abstract.en: Picture a second pair of eyes that arrives exactly when the first pair tires.
abstract.cn: 想象第二双眼恰好在第一双眼疲倦时到来。

examples.en: The lab works under the supervision of a senior researcher.
examples.cn: 实验室在一位资深研究员的监督下运作。

examples.en: Supervision of the site was split between two engineers.
examples.cn: 工地的监督由两名工程师分担。

examples.en: After the audit, supervision of all payments moved to the finance office.
examples.cn: 审计之后，所有付款的监督移交给了财务办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super（在上）+ vision（看）」——从上面看着，就是监督

root: 中世纪拉丁 supervisus（supervidere「巡视」的分词）+ -ion（动作名词后缀）；同根词有 supervise、supervisor、vision、survey。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one watching arrangement: the act of watching, the state of being watched, a student's long project, an industry's rules, an exam room, a counsellor's cases, a building site and a child at play.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一套看管安排：看这个动作、被看的状态、学生的长期研究、行业的规则、考场、咨询师的个案、工地，以及在院子里玩的孩子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lamp above every bench, so no corner of the work stays dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯照着每张工作台，工作的任何角落都不留在暗处。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: watching, and being watched, are the two sides of one arrangement.
branches.cn: 动作与状态：看与被看，是同一套安排的两面。

branches.en: LONG RESEARCH: months of work are watched through regular meetings.
branches.cn: 长期研究：数月的工作靠定期会面来照看。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRY'S RULES: when the state holds the eye, watching becomes regulation.
branches.cn: 行业规则：当国家握着这只眼，看管就变成监管。

branches.en: PLACES WITH FIXED RULES: an exam hall and a gas connection both need more than one visit.
branches.cn: 有固定规则的地点：考场与燃气接管都需要不止一次到场。

branches.en: CARE RATHER THAN POLICING: a counsellor and a child are watched in order to help.
branches.cn: 照料而非纠察：咨询师与孩子被看着，是为了帮他们。

intro.en: Supervision is the noun of a Latin verb of looking over, and its endings and roots both appear across English.
intro.cn: supervision 是一个表示「从上方看」的拉丁动词的名词，其词尾与词根在英语中都有多处出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin super gives superstructure and superimpose; videre gives vision, visible and evident.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 super 衍生 superstructure（上部结构）与 superimpose（叠加）；videre 衍生 vision（视觉）、visible（可见的）与 evident（明显的）。

items.example: The prefix sets the eye above the work.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把眼置于工作之上。

items.example: The compound is the medieval source.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是中世纪的源头。

items.example: The verb is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词是这个名词的基座。

items.meaning: the act or arrangement of watching
items.example: The ending turns the act into an institution.
The agent noun names the eye.
The same root also names sight itself.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根也命名「看见」本身。

items.example: The cousin looks over land instead of staff.
items.exampleCN: 这位表亲巡视的是土地而不是员工。

definition_zh: 监督者；主管；导师；（美国部分地区的）县政委员；监考人
definition_en: a person who watches over other workers or a process and is responsible for it
core_image: 一个站在工序尽头的人，手里拿着清单，逐项核对刚做完的东西
scene: 流水线末端的检查台上，每件成品都要经过同一个人复核，合格才盖章。A supervisor checks the last item before the line stops for the night.
sceneCN: 这里 supervisor 指对他人工作或流程负监督之责的人（第 1 个义项：直接看管工人的人）；句意：产线夜里停工前，主管检查最后一件产品。图中可辨识物件：检查台、成品、印章、交接记录。

pos.zh: 监督者；主管；导师；监考人；（美国）县政委员

senses.title: The one who watches the workers
senses.definition: a person whose job is to watch other workers and see that the work is done properly
senses.definitionCN: 受雇看住其他工人并确保工作做好的那个人
senses.example: The supervisor stopped the line when she saw the wrong label.
senses.exampleCN: 主管看到标签贴错，就叫停了产线。
senses.why: The word is the agent form of supervise, so it names the eye that sits above the work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 supervise 的施动形式，命名的是悬在工作上方的那只眼。

senses.title: Head of a shift or unit
senses.titleCN: 一个班次或单元的主管
senses.definition: the person in charge of one shift, counter or small unit during working hours
senses.definitionCN: 在工作时段内负责一个班次、柜台或小单元的人
senses.example: The night-shift supervisor counts the keys before handing over.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班主管在交接前清点钥匙。
senses.why: A shift is a closed block of time, and one person must answer for that block.
senses.whyCN: 一个班次是一段封闭的时间，必须有人为这一段负责。

senses.title: Academic research adviser
senses.definition: a teacher who guides a student's research and approves its progress
senses.definitionCN: 指导学生研究并核可其进度的一位教师
senses.example: Her supervisor asked for a shorter literature review.
senses.exampleCN: 她的导师要求把文献综述写短一些。
senses.why: Research has no shift and no counter, so the same eye is lent to one student for years.
senses.whyCN: 研究没有班次也没有柜台，于是同一只眼借给一个学生好几年。

senses.title: An elected county official
senses.definition: in some American states, an elected member of a county's governing board
senses.definitionCN: 在美国某些州，县管理委员会的民选成员
senses.example: The county supervisor voted against the new landfill.
senses.exampleCN: 那位县政委员投票反对新建填埋场。
senses.why: Local government borrowed the title for an officer who watches over county business.
senses.whyCN: 地方政府借用了这个称号，指看管县务的官员。

senses.title: An examination invigilator
senses.definition: the person who watches candidates during an examination
senses.definitionCN: 考试期间看住考生的人
senses.example: The supervisor read the rules before opening the envelopes.
senses.exampleCN: 监考人在拆封前宣读了考场规则。
senses.why: An exam is a guarded room, and the guard is called by the watching word.
senses.whyCN: 考场是一个被守住的房间，守门人就用那个表示「看」的词来称呼。

senses.title: A program that controls other programs
senses.definition: a controlling program that starts, stops and watches other processes
senses.definitionCN: 负责启动、停止并监视其他进程的控制程序
senses.example: The supervisor restarts any worker that crashes.
senses.exampleCN: 监控程序会重启任何崩溃的工作进程。
senses.why: When software took over the watching, the name of the person passed to the program.
senses.whyCN: 当软件接手「看管」，人的名称就传给了程序。

senses.title: The hospital officer who allocates beds
senses.titleCN: 在医院调度床位与人员的主管
senses.definition: the nursing officer who coordinates beds and staffing across a hospital at night
senses.definitionCN: 夜间统筹全院床位与护理人力的护理主管
senses.example: The house supervisor found a bed for the second ambulance.
senses.exampleCN: 值班主管为第二辆救护车找到了床位。
senses.why: A whole hospital at night is one closed block, and one watching officer keeps it balanced.
senses.whyCN: 夜里的整座医院是一个封闭单元，由一位值班主管让它保持平衡。

senses.title: A visit monitor in social services
senses.titleCN: 社会福利中监督探视的人
senses.definition: a person who watches a court-ordered family visit to keep everyone safe
senses.definitionCN: 在法院指定的家庭探视中在场监督、保障各方安全的人
senses.example: A supervisor sat in the corner during the two-hour visit.
senses.exampleCN: 两小时的探视中，一位监督员坐在角落。
senses.why: Here the eye protects rather than judges, which is the guarding side of the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这里的眼睛是保护而非评判，这正是同一个词里「守护」的那一面。

intro.en: Supervisor is the agent noun of supervise, from Medieval Latin supervisus 'looked over'. Its many job senses all keep one picture: an eye placed above a piece of work.
intro.cn: supervisor 是 supervise 的施动名词，源自中世纪拉丁 supervisus「被巡视过的」。它的众多职位义都保留同一个画面：一只眼悬在一项工作的上方。

items.en: Videre 'to see' gives the vis- of supervisor, and also vision and visible.
items.cn: videre「看见」提供了 supervisor 里的 vis-，也提供 vision 与 visible。

items.en: Super 'above' places the watcher higher than the watched, which is why the title carries authority.
items.cn: super「在上」把看的人放在被看者之上，因此这个称号带有权力。

items.en: Supervidere 'to inspect' produced the participle supervisus and the agent form supervisor in medieval Latin.
items.cn: supervidere「检查」在中世纪拉丁产生分词 supervisus 与施动形式 supervisor。

items.en: Supervisor appears in English in the sixteenth century, at first for an inspector of work; the earliest date is approximate.
items.cn: supervisor 在十六世纪出现于英语，最初指工作的检查者；最早年代为约数。

items.en: County boards, hospitals and computing gave the title new offices in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 县政委员会、医院与计算机在十九、二十世纪赋予这个称号新的职位。

note.en: The first group shares the supervise root or a near shape; the second group names other people who check work.
note.cn: 第一组共享 supervise 词根或形音相近；第二组是其他核查工作的人。

entries.definition: The verb, naming the activity rather than the person.
The activity or the state of being watched over.
entries.definitionCN: 指监督活动或被监督的状态。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the role or its powers.
entries.definitionCN: 描述该角色或其权力的形容词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb, but the person measures land rather than staff.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个拉丁动词，但此人是丈量土地，不是看人。

entries.definition: Runs a unit and its results; a supervisor may only check that rules are kept.
entries.definitionCN: 经营一个单元及其成果；主管可能只核查规则是否遵守。

entries.definition: The English-rooted word for the same role, often on plantations or worksites.
entries.definitionCN: 同一角色的英语本族词，常用于种植园或工地。

entries.definition: The working leader of a gang of manual workers.
entries.definitionCN: 一组体力工人中带班的领头人。

entries.definition: The British title for the person who watches an examination.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中监考人的称号。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real agent suffix, the real family and real job titles.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的施动后缀、真实的同族词与真实的职位名称。

normal.en: Supervise plus -or gives supervisor, literally the one who looks over.
normal.cn: supervise 加施动后缀得到 supervisor，字面上就是「在上方看的那一个」。

normal.en: The family runs supervise, supervision, supervisory and supervisorship.
normal.cn: 同族词有 supervise、supervision、supervisory 与 supervisorship。

normal.en: Titles show the range: shift supervisor, site supervisor, research supervisor.
normal.cn: 职位显示它的范围：值班主管、现场主管、研究导师。

normal.en: The vis- inside means seeing, which is why a supervisor is first an eye.
normal.cn: 其中的 vis- 意为看见，因此主管首先是一只眼。

normal.en: In computing the same name passed from the person to a program.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，同一个名称从人传给了程序。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that touches nothing but marks each finished piece with a stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手什么也不碰，只给每件成品盖一个章。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp at the end of a tunnel that lights each worker as they pass.
abstract.cn: 想象隧道尽头的一盏灯，照着每个经过的工人。

abstract.en: Picture a list where every line is already ticked before the shift ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一张清单，班次结束前每行都已画了勾。

examples.en: Her supervisor signed off the report after one revision.
examples.cn: 她的导师在改过一稿后签批了报告。

examples.en: The shift supervisor sent two workers home early.
examples.cn: 值班主管让两名工人提前回家。

examples.en: A floor supervisor walks the aisles before the store opens.
examples.cn: 开店前，卖场主管会走一遍货架通道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「super（在上）+ visor（看的人）」——在上面看着的人，就是主管

root: 中世纪拉丁 supervisus（supervidere「巡视」的过去分词）+ 施动后缀；同根词有 supervise、supervision、vision。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one eye at work: it watches a crew, holds one shift, guides one student, sits on a county board, guards an exam, controls other programs, balances a hospital at night and protects a family visit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都让一只眼留在工作现场：看住工班、守住一个班次、带一个学生、坐在县政委员会、守住考场、控制其他程序、夜里平衡整座医院、保护一次家庭探视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at the end of the line with a list, ticking each finished item.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着清单站在产线末端，逐项打勾。

branches.en: THE CREW AND THE SHIFT: the same eye, once on the work and once on the clock.
branches.cn: 工班与班次：同一只眼，一次看活，一次看钟。

branches.en: THE STUDENT: the eye is lent to one person for years.
branches.cn: 学生：这只眼借给一个人好几年。

branches.en: THE COUNTY BOARD: local government borrows the title.
branches.cn: 县政委员会：地方政府借用了这个称号。

branches.en: THE GUARDED AND THE PROTECTED: an exam is watched to keep rules, a visit to keep people safe.
branches.cn: 看守与保护：监考为守规则，探视为保安全。

branches.en: THE MACHINE AND THE WARD: a program and a night officer both keep many parts in balance.
branches.cn: 机器与病区：一个程序与一位夜班主管都在让众多部分保持平衡。

intro.en: Supervisor is supervise plus an agent ending, and the seeing root behind it also builds words about sight and inspection.
intro.cn: supervisor 是 supervise 加上施动词尾，其背后的「看见」词根还构成与视觉、检查有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre gives vision, visible and evident; supervidere gives supervise, supervision and survey.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 videre 衍生 vision、visible 与 evident；supervidere 衍生 supervise、supervision 与 survey。

items.example: The prefix places the eye above the work.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把眼放在工作上方。

items.example: The compound is the medieval source.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是中世纪以来的源头。

items.example: The verb is the base of this noun.
items.exampleCN: 动词是这个名词的基座。

items.example: The action noun sits beside the person noun.
items.exampleCN: 动作名词与人名词并列。

items.example: The suffix names the office, not the person.
The cousin word keeps the same eye.
items.exampleCN: 这位表亲保留同一只眼。

definition_en: something added to improve or complete another thing
core_image: 一杯水旁放着一片维生素，补足饮食的缺口
scene: 这种药片是维生素补充剂。This tablet is a vitamin supplement.
sceneCN: 这里 supplement 是「补充物、补充剂」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这种药片是维生素补充剂。

senses.title: Something added
senses.definition: something added to complete or improve
senses.definitionCN: 为补全或改善而添加的东西
senses.example: This tablet is a vitamin supplement.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药片是维生素补充剂。
senses.why: This is the main noun sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的名词义项。

senses.title: To add to something
senses.definition: to add something to improve or complete
senses.definitionCN: 添加某物以改善或补全
senses.example: She supplements her income with evening work.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠晚间工作补充收入。
senses.why: This is the verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是动词义项。

senses.title: An extra section
senses.definition: an extra part added to a newspaper or book
senses.definitionCN: 报纸或书籍附加的部分
senses.example: The newspaper printed a weekend supplement.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸印了一份周末增刊。
senses.why: Here the added thing is a publication.
senses.whyCN: 这里添加的是出版物。

intro.en: Supplement comes from Latin supplere, to fill up.
intro.cn: supplement 来自拉丁语 supplere，意为填满、补足。

items.en: Sub meant under.
Plere meant to fill.
Supplementum meant something added.
Supplement meant an addition.
Supplement meant a pill or an extra part.
items.cn: supplement 指补充剂或附加部分。

note.en: Supplement is compared with its look-alike complement and with words for additions.
note.cn: 把 supplement 与形近的 complement 以及表示添加物的词作比较。

entries.definition: something added to a main thing

normalIntro.en: A supplement fills a gap that the main thing leaves open.
normalIntro.cn: supplement 补上主要事物留下的缺口。

normal.en: This tablet is a vitamin supplement.
normal.cn: 这种药片是维生素补充剂。

normal.en: She supplements her income with evening work.
normal.cn: 她靠晚间工作补充收入。

normal.en: The newspaper printed a weekend supplement.
normal.cn: 报纸印了一份周末增刊。

normal.en: He takes an iron supplement daily.
normal.cn: 他每天服用铁补充剂。

normal.en: The course is a supplement to the main textbook.
normal.cn: 这门课是主教材的补充。

abstract.en: A supplement is a bridge over a small gap.
abstract.cn: 补充物，是架在小缺口上的一座桥。

abstract.en: What completes us is not always what replaces us.
abstract.cn: 补全我们的，不一定是取代我们的。

abstract.en: Good supplements know when to stop.
abstract.cn: 好的补充，懂得何时停止。

examples.en: This tablet is a vitamin supplement.
examples.cn: 这种药片是维生素补充剂。

examples.en: She supplements her income with evening work.
examples.cn: 她靠晚间工作补充收入。

examples.en: The newspaper printed a weekend supplement.
examples.cn: 报纸印了一份周末增刊。

dict_mnemonic.text: supplement 是「补充物」，作动词表示补充；vitamin supplement 是维生素补充剂，supplementary 是补充的。注意与 complement（补全）区分。

root: 来自拉丁语 supplere（填满），由 sub（在下）与 plere（填满）组成，字面是「在下面填满」，引申为补充。

sensesIntro.en: Supplement means something added to complete a thing, the act of adding, or an extra publication section.
sensesIntro.cn: supplement 表示补全某物的添加物、补充的动作，或报刊的增刊。

core.en: An addition that fills a gap.
core.cn: 填补缺口的添加。

branches.en: This tablet is a vitamin supplement.
branches.cn: 这种药片是维生素补充剂。

branches.en: She supplements her income with evening work.
branches.cn: 她靠晚间工作补充收入。

branches.en: The newspaper printed a weekend supplement.
branches.cn: 报纸印了一份周末增刊。

branches.en: The thing added and the act of adding share a word.
branches.cn: 添加物与添加动作共用一个词。

branches.en: The course is a supplement to the main textbook.
branches.cn: 这门课是主教材的补充。

intro.en: Supplement builds supplementary and supplementation.
intro.cn: supplement 可构成 supplementary 和 supplementation。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin plere, to fill, with sub under.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 plere（填满），加上 sub（在下）。

latinEntries.example: Supplere is the source of supplement.
latinEntries.exampleCN: supplere 是 supplement 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Plere also gave English complete.
latinEntries.exampleCN: plere 也演变为英语的 complete。

definition_zh: 供应商；供货方；供应者；（古）补足者
definition_en: a person or company that provides goods or services that others need
core_image: 一辆装满货箱的卡车停在仓库门口，把空掉的货架补满
scene: 仓库的货架空了，一辆卡车停在门口，司机把装箱单递给采购员。The driver works for a supplier of machine parts.
sceneCN: 这里 supplier 是「供应商」（第 1 个义项：向其他企业提供货物的公司）；句意：这位司机为一家机器零件供应商工作。

derivatives.zh: 供应；提供（supplier 的基础动词与名词）
供应品；补给（supply 的复数名词）
供应；供货（动词 supply 的动名词）

senses.title: A company that provides goods
senses.definition: a company that sells goods to another company or shop
senses.definitionCN: 向另一家公司或商店出售货物的公司
senses.example: The factory ordered parts from three suppliers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂向三家供应商订购了零件。
senses.why: Supplier is the agent noun of supply, so the core image is one who fills what another lacks.
senses.whyCN: supplier 是 supply 的施动名词，核心意象就是「把别人缺的东西补齐的人」。

senses.title: A provider of a service or resource
senses.definition: a person or organization that provides a service, energy, or water to users
senses.definitionCN: 向用户提供服务、能源或水的个人或组织
senses.example: The energy supplier cut off the gas to the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 这家能源供应商切断了整条街的燃气。
senses.why: The agent noun extends from goods to any continuous resource that is delivered.
senses.whyCN: 这个施动名词从货物扩展到任何持续输送的资源。

senses.title: The party that supplies under a contract
senses.definition: the party in a commercial contract who must provide the goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 商业合同中必须提供货物或服务的一方
senses.example: If the supplier delivers late, the buyer may claim damages.
senses.exampleCN: 如果供货方延迟交货，买方可以要求赔偿损失。
senses.why: Contract law fixes the general provider into a named role with duties.
senses.whyCN: 合同法把一般的供应者固定成一个有明确义务的角色。

senses.title: A person who provides something needed
senses.definition: a person who gives or provides something that others need
senses.definitionCN: 向他人提供所需之物的个人
senses.example: Her uncle was a supplier of books to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 她的叔叔曾是村里学校的图书供应者。
senses.why: Behind the company sense stands the simple human act of handing over what is needed.
senses.whyCN: 在公司义项背后，是「把需要的东西交出去」这一简单的人类行为。

senses.title: One who fills a lack
senses.definition: an old sense: one who fills up or completes what is missing
senses.definitionCN: 古义：把缺少的东西填满或补全的人
senses.example: In older texts a supplier was one who filled a vacancy.
senses.exampleCN: 在更早的文本里，supplier 指填补空缺的人。
senses.why: The Latin source supplere means to fill up, and the oldest agent sense keeps that image of completing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源 supplere 意为填满，最早的施动义保留了「补全」的意象。

intro.en: Supplier comes from supply, from Old French souploier, to fill up, from Latin supplere, to complete.
intro.cn: supplier 来自 supply，源于古法语 souploier（填满），再往前是拉丁语 supplere（补足）。

items.en: Supplere means to fill up or make complete.
It joins sub, from below, and plere, to fill.
items.cn: 它由 sub（从下）与 plere（填满）组合而成。

items.en: Souploier carries the sense of filling a need.
items.cn: souploier 承袭了「满足需要、补足」的含义。

items.en: Supply enters English as a verb meaning to fill or provide.
items.cn: supply 以动词身份进入英语，意为填补或提供。

items.en: The agent noun supplier names the one who provides.
items.cn: 施动名词 supplier 指提供货物的一方。

items.en: Supplier becomes a standard word for business vendors.
items.cn: supplier 成为商业中对供货方的标准称呼。

note.en: Supplier is the agent noun of supply, close to the verb, its forms, and to words for sellers.
note.cn: supplier 是 supply 的施动名词，与动词本身、其变形以及表示售卖者的词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 出售货物的公司；供应商

entries.definition: a person or company that provides a service
entries.definitionCN: 提供服务或资源的个人或公司

entries.definition: a person who buys and sells goods

normalIntro.en: Supplier is supply plus the agent ending, the one who fills an order.
normalIntro.cn: supplier 是 supply 加上表示施动者的词尾，指把订单补齐的一方。

normal.en: Supply comes from a Latin verb meaning to fill up.
normal.cn: supply 来自意为「填满」的拉丁语动词。

normal.en: A supplier fills the gap in another company stock.
normal.cn: 供应商填补另一家公司库存的空缺。

normal.en: The ending -ier marks the person or firm that does the supplying.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ier 标记执行供应的人或公司。

normal.en: An energy supplier delivers gas or power to homes.
normal.cn: 能源供应商向家庭输送燃气或电力。

normal.en: In a contract the supplier is the party who must deliver.
normal.cn: 在合同里，supplier 是必须交货的一方。

abstract.en: Picture a truck loading boxes into an empty warehouse.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆卡车把箱子装进空仓库。

abstract.en: Imagine a pipe that carries water into every kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根把水送进每家厨房的管道。

abstract.en: Think of a signed page where one party promises to deliver.
abstract.cn: 想象一页签好的文件，其中一方承诺交货。

examples.en: The bakery buys its flour from a local supplier.
examples.cn: 这家面包店从本地供应商那里购买面粉。

examples.en: Our supplier failed to deliver the order on time.
examples.cn: 我们的供应商未能按时交付订单。

examples.en: The hospital chose a new supplier of medical gloves.
examples.cn: 医院选定了新的医用手套供应商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「苏普莱尔」——supply（供应）加上「人」，就是供货的人；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（从下往上）+ plere（填满）→ supplere（补足）→ 古法语 souploier → 英语 supply → supplier（供应者），核心义「把缺的东西补齐」。

sensesIntro.en: Supplier starts as the agent noun of supply, naming the firm that provides goods, then any provider of a resource, then the contract party, and finally the older filler of a lack.
sensesIntro.cn: supplier 先是 supply 的施动名词，指向企业提供货物，再指资源供应方、合同供货方，最后保留「补足者」的古义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a truck filling the empty shelves of a warehouse.
core.cn: 核心意象：卡车把空货架重新填满。

branches.en: The goods supplier is the everyday business sense.
branches.cn: 货物供应商是最日常的商业义项。

branches.en: A resource provider extends the filling image to services.
branches.cn: 资源供应方把「填满」的意象扩展到服务。

branches.en: The contract party turns the provider into a legal role.
branches.cn: 合同供货方把供应者变成法律角色。

branches.en: Both goods and services are delivered to fill a need.
branches.cn: 货物与服务都是为填补需要而交付的。

branches.en: The provider, the contract party, and the old filler all complete a gap.
branches.cn: 供应者、合同供货方与古老义项中的补足者，都在补上一个缺口。

intro.en: Supplier grows from the Latin verb supplere, to fill up, through English supply and the agent suffix -ier.
intro.cn: supplier 从拉丁语动词 supplere（补足）经英语 supply 与施动词尾 -ier 发展而来。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplere means to fill up, built from sub, below, and plere, to fill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supplere 意为填满，由 sub（在下）与 plere（填满）构成。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 开启 supplere 一词。

items.example: Supplere is the direct source of supply.
items.exampleCN: supplere 是 supply 的直接来源。

items.example: Supply is the base of supplier.
items.exampleCN: supply 是 supplier 的基础词。
supplier 指提供货物的公司。

items.example: Supplementum is the Latin noun of supplere.
items.exampleCN: supplementum 是 supplere 的拉丁名词。

definition_en: to provide something needed, or the amount provided
core_image: 一辆货车把新鲜蔬菜卸到商店门口
scene: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
sceneCN: 这里 supply 是「供应」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。

senses.title: To provide
senses.definition: to give or sell something that is needed
senses.definitionCN: 给出或出售所需要的东西
senses.example: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
senses.exampleCN: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。
senses.why: This is the main verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的动词义项。

senses.title: The amount available
senses.definition: the amount of something available
senses.definitionCN: 可获得的东西的数量
senses.example: The water supply is limited.
senses.exampleCN: 供水是有限的。
senses.why: Here the word is a noun of amount.
senses.whyCN: 这里指数量的名词。

senses.title: Goods for a need
senses.definition: food and equipment needed for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某一目的需要的食物与装备
senses.example: They carried medical supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 他们携带医疗物资。
senses.why: This plural sense names concrete goods.
senses.whyCN: 这个复数义项指具体物资。

intro.en: Supply comes from Latin supplere, to fill up.
intro.cn: supply 来自拉丁语 supplere，意为填满、补足。

items.en: Sub meant under.
Plere meant to fill.
Suppleer meant to fill a need.
Supply meant to provide.

note.en: Supply is compared with look-alike words and with verbs of providing.

entries.definition: to ask formally or to put on

normalIntro.en: To supply is to fill the empty space in someone's need.
normalIntro.cn: supply 就是填满别人需求里的空位。

normal.en: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.
normal.cn: 这家农场向本地商店供应蔬菜。

normal.en: The water supply is limited.
normal.cn: 供水是有限的。

normal.en: They carried medical supplies.
normal.cn: 他们携带医疗物资。

normal.en: Demand is rising faster than supply.
normal.cn: 需求的增长快于供应。

normal.en: Fresh water is in short supply here.
normal.cn: 这里淡水供应不足。

abstract.en: Supply is a promise made in goods.
abstract.cn: 供应，是用货物许下的承诺。

abstract.en: What is in short supply becomes precious.
abstract.cn: 供应不足的东西会变得珍贵。

abstract.en: A chain of supply is a chain of trust.
abstract.cn: 供应链，也是一条信任链。

examples.en: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.

sensesIntro.en: Supply means to provide something needed, the amount available, or the goods provided.
sensesIntro.cn: supply 表示提供所需之物、可获得的供应量，或所提供的物资。

core.en: Filling a need with goods.

branches.en: The farm supplies vegetables to local shops.

branches.en: They carried medical supplies.

branches.en: The act and the amount share one word.
branches.cn: 供应动作与供应量共用一个词。

branches.en: Fresh water is in short supply here.

intro.en: Supply builds supplier and supplies, and shares a root with supplement.
intro.cn: supply 可构成 supplier 和 supplies，并与 supplement 同根。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin plere, to fill.

latinEntries.example: Supplere is the source of supply.

latinEntries.example: Plere also gave English complete.

definition_en: to help or hold something up, or to provide for someone
core_image: 两根柱子稳稳托住屋顶
scene: 家人支持她的决定。Her family supported her decision.
sceneCN: 这里 support 是「支持」（第 1 个义项）；句意：家人支持她的决定。

senses.title: To back someone
senses.definition: to help someone or agree with a plan
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某人或赞成某个计划
senses.example: Her family supported her decision.
senses.exampleCN: 家人支持她的决定。
senses.why: This is the main social sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的社会关系义项。

senses.title: To hold up
senses.definition: to carry the weight of something
senses.definitionCN: 承受某物的重量
senses.example: The columns support the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这些柱子支撑着屋顶。
senses.why: This is the physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理义项。

senses.title: Help or a prop
senses.definition: help given, or a thing that holds something up
senses.definitionCN: 给予的帮助，或托住某物的东西
senses.example: The bridge needs more support.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥需要更多支撑。
senses.why: This noun covers help and structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖帮助与支撑结构。

senses.title: To provide for

definition_zh: 压制；镇压；抑制；忍住；隐瞒；抑制（生理反应）
definition_en: to put something down by force, to hold it back from expression or release, and to keep it from being known
core_image: 桌上立着一根弹簧，一只手把它压到桌面，弹簧在掌下弯成扁弧，一松手就会弹起
scene: 桌上立着一根弹簧，一只手把它压到桌面，弹簧在掌下弯成扁弧，一松手就会弹起。The officer tried to suppress the disturbance before it spread.
sceneCN: 这里指以力量制止、镇压（第 1 个义项：用武力压住骚乱）；句意为那名官员试图在骚乱扩散之前把它压制住。

pos.zh: 压制；镇压；抑制；忍住；隐瞒

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加表示动作结果的名词尾构成，义为「压制；抑制；隐瞒」
由该动词加表示施动者或装置的名词尾构成，义为「压制者；抑制器」
由该动词加表示起某作用之物的词尾构成，义为「抑制剂（尤指止咳药）」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被压制的」
由该动词加表示性质的形容词尾构成，义为「压制的；抑制性的」

senses.title: Put down a revolt by force
senses.definition: to end an uprising, riot or disturbance using authority or armed force
senses.definitionCN: 用权威或武力结束暴动、骚乱或动乱
senses.example: Troops were sent to suppress the revolt.
senses.exampleCN: 军队被派去镇压叛乱。
senses.why: The Latin compound means to press from below, and a force that presses a crowd down is the oldest sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁复合词意为「从下面压」，而把人群压下去的力量，正是这个词最古老的义项。

senses.title: Hold back an expression of feeling
senses.definition: to stop a smile, laugh, tear or cry from showing or escaping
senses.definitionCN: 阻止笑、哭或眼泪表现出来或发出
senses.example: She could not suppress a smile at the joke.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个笑话，她忍不住笑了。
senses.why: A feeling pushes upward like a spring, and suppressing it is the hand that keeps the spring compressed.
senses.whyCN: 情绪像弹簧一样向上顶，而「抑制」就是那只把弹簧压住的手。

senses.title: Hold back a bodily reflex
senses.definition: to prevent a cough, sneeze or yawn from happening or being heard
senses.definitionCN: 阻止咳嗽、打喷嚏或打哈欠发生或被听见
senses.example: He tried to suppress a cough during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间他努力忍住咳嗽。
senses.why: Here the body itself is the spring, and the will is the hand pressing it down for a while.
senses.whyCN: 这里身体本身就是那根弹簧，而意志是暂时把它压住的手。

senses.title: Keep information from the public
senses.definition: to prevent a report, fact or image from being published or circulated
senses.definitionCN: 阻止报道、事实或图像被发表或传播
senses.example: The government tried to suppress the report.
senses.exampleCN: 政府试图压下那份报告。
senses.why: What is pressed down cannot rise into view, so the word moved from crowds to facts that someone wants buried.
senses.whyCN: 被压住的东西无法升到眼前，于是这个词从人群转到有人想埋掉的事实。

senses.title: Hold back growth
senses.definition: to stop plants, cells or organisms from growing or spreading
senses.definitionCN: 阻止植物、细胞或生物生长或蔓延
senses.example: Chemical sprays suppress the weeds along the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 化学喷剂抑制了篱笆边的杂草。
senses.why: Growth is an upward push too, and agriculture uses the same pressing image as politics.
senses.whyCN: 生长同样是一种向上的推力，农业用的也是政治里那同一个「压」的意象。

senses.title: Reduce a biological response
senses.definition: in medicine and biology, to weaken an immune, inflammatory or nervous response
senses.definitionCN: 医学与生物学中指减弱免疫、炎症或神经反应
senses.example: The drug suppresses the immune response.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药抑制免疫反应。
senses.why: A response that has been damped down is literally held back, which is exactly what the Latin verb says.
senses.whyCN: 被压低的反应字面上就是被按住，这正是那个拉丁动词所说的。

senses.title: Reduce sound or vibration
senses.definition: to lessen noise, echo or shaking produced by a machine or a room
senses.definitionCN: 减弱机器或房间产生的噪音、回声或震动
senses.example: New panels were fitted to suppress the engine noise.
senses.exampleCN: 安装了新面板以压制发动机噪音。
senses.why: Sound is a wave that pushes outward, and damping it is another version of pressing down.
senses.whyCN: 声音是向外推的波，把它减弱又是「压下去」的另一种版本。

senses.title: Keep evidence from being seen
senses.definition: to hide a document, witness or fact that would otherwise come before a court
senses.definitionCN: 藏起本会呈上法庭的文件、证人或事实
senses.example: The company was accused of suppressing evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司被指控隐瞒证据。
senses.why: The legal sense sharpens the secrecy sense: what is suppressed is not destroyed but kept from surfacing.
senses.whyCN: 法律义把「隐瞒」义磨得更锋利：被压下的东西不是被销毁，而是被阻止浮出水面。

senses.title: Put out a fire
senses.definition: to stop a fire or flame from spreading by smothering or cooling it
senses.definitionCN: 用窒息或降温的方式阻止火或火焰蔓延
senses.example: Firefighters worked fast to suppress the blaze.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员迅速行动扑灭大火。
senses.why: Fire is the most visible thing that spreads upward, and putting it out is the word at its most physical.
senses.whyCN: 火是最显眼的向上蔓延之物，把火扑灭正是这个词最物理的一面。

intro.en: Suppress comes from Latin suppressus, the past participle of supprimere, to press down, built from sub-, under, and premere, to press.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 suppressus，即 supprimere「向下压」的过去分词，由 sub-「在下」与 premere「压」构成。

items.en: Premere meant to press, squeeze or stamp, and its family includes press and imprint.
items.cn: premere 意为压、挤或印，其同族包括「压」与「印痕」等词。

items.en: The compound added the idea of downward pressure, and it could describe both a foot on a thing and a force on a people.
items.cn: 这个复合词加上向下的压力，既能描述脚踩在某物上，也能描述力量压在人群上。

items.en: The participle meant pressed down or held back, and English took it as an adjective before it took it as a verb.
items.cn: 这个分词意为被压下、被按住的，英语先把它作形容词用，再作动词用。

items.en: The verb entered English in the late Middle Ages with the political sense first; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在中世纪末进入英语，最先带的正是政治义；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Medicine extended the word to coughs, immune responses and hormones that the body itself holds back.
items.cn: 医学把词扩展到咳嗽、免疫反应与身体自身会抑制的激素。

items.en: Journalism gave the word its common modern sense of keeping a story out of sight.
items.cn: 新闻业赋予它常见的现代义：把一则报道挡在视线之外。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like suppress; the second group names neighbouring ways of holding something down.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 suppress 相近；第二组是与「压住、止住」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of putting something down or keeping it from showing.
entries.definitionCN: 指压制、抑制或隐瞒的行为。

entries.definition: A person or device that holds something back.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行压制的人或装置。

entries.definition: A substance that reduces a bodily function, especially a cough.
entries.definitionCN: 指减弱身体功能的物质，尤指止咳药。

entries.definition: Acting to hold something down or reduce it.
entries.definitionCN: 指起压制或减弱作用的。

entries.definition: To think something is likely; it shares the prefix but rests on a verb meaning to place.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为某事很可能；共享前缀，但底层是意为「放置」的动词。

entries.definition: To push a feeling or memory back so that it does not enter awareness; it stresses the inward push.
entries.definitionCN: 指把情绪或记忆压回去使其不进入意识；强调向内的推压。

entries.definition: To keep people under harsh control over a long time; it stresses the weight on the group.
entries.definitionCN: 指长期以严酷方式统治人群；强调压在群体身上的重量。

entries.definition: To hold someone or something back from acting; it stresses the leash rather than the weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻止某人或某物行动；强调缰绳而非重量。

entries.definition: To put down a disturbance or a strong feeling; close to the first sense but more literary.
entries.definitionCN: 指平息骚动或强烈情绪；接近第一个义项，但更书面。

entries.definition: To cut off the air or the expression of something; it stresses suffocation more than pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指切断空气或某种表达；强调窒息感而非压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pressing root, the downward prefix and the many objects the word has been applied to.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「压」的词根、向下的前缀，以及这个词曾被用到的众多对象。

normal.en: The prefix means under and the verb means press, so the word says press under.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「在下」，词根意为「压」，所以这个词说的就是「往下压」。

normal.en: A hand on a spring is the picture: hold it down and it cannot jump.
normal.cn: 手压弹簧就是那幅图：按住它，它就弹不起来。

normal.en: A cough suppressant does to a cough what a lid does to a flame.
normal.cn: 止咳药对咳嗽做的事，就像盖子对火焰做的事。

normal.en: A suppressed report is a report someone is sitting on.
normal.cn: 被压下的报道，就是有人坐在上面的报道。

normal.en: The word covers crowds, smiles, coughs, weeds, immune cells, noise, evidence and fire, all by the same downward gesture.
normal.cn: 这个词覆盖人群、笑容、咳嗽、杂草、免疫细胞、噪音、证据与火焰，靠的都是同一个向下压的手势。

abstract.en: Suppression works by making something invisible rather than by making it cease to exist.
abstract.cn: 压制靠的是让某物看不见，而不是让它不再存在。

abstract.en: What is held down keeps its energy; release it and the spring jumps.
abstract.cn: 被压住的东西保留着能量；一松手，弹簧就会跳起来。

abstract.en: A society that suppresses a fact usually pays for it later in a larger disturbance.
abstract.cn: 压制事实的社会，通常要在之后以更大的动荡付出代价。

examples.en: The regime suppressed every paper that criticised it.
examples.cn: 该政权压制了每一份批评它的报纸。

examples.en: She suppressed a yawn and kept writing.
examples.cn: 她忍住哈欠，继续写下去。

examples.en: Doctors gave him a drug to suppress the inflammation.
examples.cn: 医生给他一种药以抑制炎症。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑟普雷斯」——「瑟」抖的弹簧被「普雷」一下压平，还「斯」的一声贴住桌面：压制

root: 拉丁语 premere「压」→ sub-「在下」+ premere 构成 supprimere「向下压」→ 过去分词 suppressus「被压住的」→ 英语 suppress「压制；抑制；隐瞒」；核心动作始终是「从上方把东西按下去」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one downward gesture: a revolt, a smile, a cough, a report, weeds, an immune response, noise, evidence and a fire.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享同一个向下压的手势：叛乱、笑容、咳嗽、报道、杂草、免疫反应、噪音、证据与火焰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm pressing a standing spring flat against the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手掌把立着的弹簧压平在桌面上。

branches.en: THE FORCE BRANCH: troops end a revolt, and firefighters end a blaze.
branches.cn: 武力分支：军队平息叛乱，消防员扑灭大火。

branches.en: THE HELD-BACK BRANCH: a smile is kept in and a cough is kept down.
branches.cn: 忍住分支：笑容被收住，咳嗽被压下。

branches.en: THE SECRECY BRANCH: a report is buried and evidence is kept from court.
branches.cn: 隐瞒分支：报道被埋掉，证据被挡在法庭之外。

branches.en: THE BIOLOGY BRANCH: sprays hold weeds back and drugs damp an immune response.
branches.cn: 生物分支：喷剂抑制杂草，药物压低免疫反应。

branches.en: THE NOISE BRANCH: panels take the push out of engine sound.
branches.cn: 噪音分支：面板卸掉发动机声音里的推力。

intro.en: Suppress is a Latin compound of under and press, and English added a full set of noun and adjective endings to it.
intro.cn: 这是一个由「在下」与「压」构成的拉丁复合词，英语又给它配上一整套名词与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the prefix sub-, the verb premere and its compound supprimere, whose participle English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供前缀 sub-、动词 premere 及其复合词 supprimere，英语借用的正是它的分词。

items.example: It gives the pressure its downward direction.
items.exampleCN: 它给这份压力一个向下的方向。

items.example: The verb is the physical core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的物理核心。

items.example: The compound already carries both the physical and the political sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词已经同时带有物理义与政治义。

definition_zh: 外科医生；外科专科医师；军医
definition_en: a doctor who treats injuries and diseases by cutting into the body
core_image: 无影灯下，一双戴手套的手稳稳握住手术刀
scene: 手术室里，主刀医生举起手，示意护士递上器械。The surgeon scrubbed in and took her place at the table.
sceneCN: 这里 surgeon 是「外科医生」（第 1 个义项：以手术为主要治疗手段的医生）；句意：外科医生刷手消毒后站到了手术台前。

pos.zh: 外科医生；外科专科医师；军医

derivatives.zh: 外科；手术；由 surgeon 去掉表人后缀构成，指这门学科与操作本身
外科的；手术的；-ical 形容词后缀，修饰与手术相关的事物
通过外科手术地；-ly 副词后缀，说明手段是手术

senses.title: A doctor who performs operations
senses.definition: a doctor trained to treat disease and injury by operating on the body
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、通过切开身体来治疗疾病与创伤的医生
senses.example: The surgeon removed the appendix in under an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生不到一小时就切除了阑尾。
senses.why: The Greek compound means hand work, and the surgeon is the one whose work is done with the hands.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语复合词意为「手的工作」，外科医生正是靠双手完成治疗的人，词义从「手工」落到「做手术的人」。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch of surgery
senses.definition: a doctor who operates only on a particular organ or part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 只对某一器官或某一部位动手术的医生
senses.example: A heart surgeon repaired the leaking valve.
senses.exampleCN: 一位心脏外科医生修补了渗漏的瓣膜。
senses.why: As surgery split into specialties, the plain word took on the narrower reading of a specialist operator.
senses.whyCN: 随着外科分成各专科，这个普通称呼也收窄为「某专科的开刀医生」。

senses.title: A doctor attached to a ship or an army
senses.titleCN: 随船军医；随军外科医生
senses.definition: in earlier use, a medical officer who sailed with a ship or served with troops
senses.definitionCN: 旧时随船航行或在军中服务的外科军医
senses.example: The ship surgeon treated the sailors during the long voyage.
senses.exampleCN: 随船外科医生在漫长的航程中为水手们治伤。
senses.why: At sea and at war the person who cut and stitched was the only trained hand aboard.
senses.whyCN: 在海上和战场上，会动刀缝合的人就是船上唯一受过训练的手，于是这个词又多了一层军中职称。

senses.title: A senior hospital surgeon in Britain
senses.definition: in British hospitals, a senior surgeon at consultant level who leads a surgical team
senses.definitionCN: 在英国医院里达到顾问级别、领导一个外科团队的高级外科医师
senses.example: She was appointed consultant surgeon at the teaching hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为这家教学医院的顾问外科医师。
senses.why: The British health service kept the plain title for its most senior operating doctors.
senses.whyCN: 英国医疗体系把最资深的开刀医生仍称作 surgeon，这个职称义便从「做手术的人」升格为院内最高级别。

intro.en: Surgeon descends from Greek kheirourgia, hand work, through Latin chirurgia and Old French.
intro.cn: surgeon 源自希腊语 kheirourgia（手工作），经拉丁语 chirurgia 与古法语进入英语。

items.en: Kheir means hand and ergon means work, so kheirourgia is work done with the hands.
items.cn: kheir 意为手，ergon 意为工作，kheirourgia 就是「用手完成的活儿」。

items.en: Kheirourgos names the man who works with his hands, later the healer who operates.
items.cn: kheirourgos 指靠双手干活的人，后来专指动刀治病的人。

items.en: Medical Latin adopts chirurgia for surgery and chirurgus for the operator.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语用 chirurgia 表示外科，用 chirurgus 表示动刀的人。

items.en: Cirurgien and surgien carry the word into French.
items.cn: cirurgien 与 surgien 把这个词带进法语。

items.en: English shortens the French form to surgien and then to surgeon.
items.cn: 英语把法语词形缩短为 surgien，再演变为 surgeon。

items.en: Surgeon becomes the standard title for an operating doctor, from a ship to a consultant.
items.cn: surgeon 成为开刀医生的标准称谓，从随船军医到顾问医师都用它。

note.en: Surgeon is the hand worker of medicine, close in form to surgery and in meaning to physician and operator.
note.cn: surgeon 是医学里「用手干活的人」，形式上接近 surgery，意义上接近 physician 与 operator。

entries.definition: the branch of medicine that treats the body by cutting
entries.definitionCN: 通过切开身体来治疗疾病的医学分支，即外科

entries.definition: relating to surgery or done by a surgeon
entries.definitionCN: 与外科或手术有关的，即外科的
通过手术的方式，即外科手术地

entries.definition: a doctor who treats illness with medicine rather than with cutting
entries.definitionCN: 主要以药物而非手术治病的医生，即内科医生

entries.definition: the person who carries out a particular procedure
entries.definitionCN: 实施某项操作的人，在手术语境里指动刀者

entries.definition: a person qualified to practise medicine
entries.definitionCN: 有资格行医的人，范围比外科医生大得多

normalIntro.en: Surgeon is built from a Greek hand plus work, and English made surgery, surgical, and surgically from the same stem.
normalIntro.cn: surgeon 由希腊语的「手」加「工作」构成，英语又用同一词干造出 surgery、surgical 与 surgically。

normal.en: Greek kheir means hand, so a surgeon is literally a hand worker.
normal.cn: 希腊语 kheir 意为手，所以外科医生字面上就是「用手干活的人」。

normal.en: Surgery is the field, surgical is the adjective, and surgeon is the person.
normal.cn: surgery 是领域，surgical 是形容词，surgeon 是那个人。

normal.en: A heart surgeon operates on the heart, while a plastic surgeon reshapes tissue.
normal.cn: 心脏外科医生在心脏上动刀，整形外科医生则重塑组织。

normal.en: On a ship the surgeon was the only person who could cut and stitch.
normal.cn: 在船上，外科医生是唯一能开刀缝合的人。

normal.en: In British hospitals a consultant surgeon is the senior operator on a team.
normal.cn: 在英国医院里，顾问外科医师是团队中资深的开刀者。

abstract.en: Picture a gloved hand closing around a scalpel under bright light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只戴着手套的手在强光下握住手术刀。

abstract.en: Imagine one narrow tray of instruments laid out for one organ only.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘窄窄的器械只为一个器官摆好。

abstract.en: Think of a lantern swinging on a wooden ship while a steady hand stitches a sailor.
abstract.cn: 想象木船上的灯晃动着，一只稳稳的手正在为水手缝合。

examples.en: The surgeon spoke to the family before the operation.
examples.cn: 手术前，外科医生和家属谈了话。

examples.en: Two surgeons worked together on the transplant.
examples.cn: 两位外科医生合作完成了这台移植手术。

examples.en: The surgical team finished in three hours.
examples.cn: 手术团队三个小时就完成了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「设诊」——surgeon 读起来像「设诊」，外科医生设诊开刀；这只是谐音联想，与希腊语 kheirourgia 无关。

root: 希腊语 kheir（手）+ ergon（工作）→ kheirourgia（手工作）→ 拉丁语 chirurgia → 古法语 cirurgien → 英语 surgeon，核心义「用手做治疗的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Surgeon starts as the hand worker who cuts, narrows to a specialist of one organ or region, extends to the doctor aboard a ship, and finally becomes a senior hospital rank in Britain.
sensesIntro.cn: surgeon 从「动手开刀的人」开始，收窄为某一器官或部位的专科医师，又延伸为随船军医，最后在英国成为院内的高级职称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gloved hand holding a scalpel under the operating light.
core.cn: 核心意象：无影灯下，戴着手套的手握住手术刀。

branches.en: The hand worker who operates is the plain everyday sense.
branches.cn: 动手开刀的人是日常最普通的义项。

branches.en: One organ, one operator gives the specialist sense.
branches.cn: 一个器官配一位开刀者，就长出了专科医师义。

branches.en: A ship or an army needs its own cutting hand.
branches.cn: 船和军队都需要自己那位会动刀的人。

branches.en: The British rank marks the most senior operator in a hospital.
branches.cn: 英式职称标出医院里最资深的开刀者。

branches.en: Any operating doctor, general or specialist, is first of all a surgeon.
branches.cn: 无论普通还是专科，开刀医生首先都是 surgeon。

intro.en: Surgeon carries Greek kheir, hand, and ergon, work, through Latin and French into a family with surgery and surgical.
intro.cn: surgeon 带着希腊语的 kheir（手）与 ergon（工作），经拉丁语和法语进入英语，并衍生出 surgery 与 surgical。

latinIntro.en: Latin chirurgia means surgery and chirurgus means the operator, both taken from the Greek compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 chirurgia 意为外科，chirurgus 意为动刀者，二者都借自那个希腊语复合词。

items.example: Kheir supplies the hand in the Greek compound.
items.exampleCN: kheir 为这个希腊语复合词提供「手」这一要素。

items.example: Ergon supplies the work in the same compound.
items.exampleCN: ergon 为同一复合词提供「工作」这一要素。

items.example: Kheirourgia is literally work done with the hands.
items.exampleCN: kheirourgia 字面就是「用手完成的活儿」。

items.example: Kheirourgos names the person who does the hand work.
Chirurgia is the Latin form of the Greek noun.
items.exampleCN: chirurgia 是这个希腊名词的拉丁语形式。

items.example: Chirurgus is the Latin name for the operator.
items.exampleCN: chirurgus 是拉丁语中对动刀者的称呼。

items.example: Cirurgien is the Old French form of the word.
items.exampleCN: cirurgien 是这个词的古法语形式。

items.example: Surgeon is the modern English form.
items.exampleCN: surgeon 是现代英语的形式。

items.example: Surgery names both the field and the act.
items.exampleCN: surgery 同时指这门学科和手术操作。

items.example: The suffix -ical forms the adjective surgical.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ical 构成形容词 surgical。

items.example: The suffix -ical builds adjectives from nouns.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ical 由名词构成形容词。

definition_en: medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body
core_image: 无影灯下，医生戴着口罩专注操作
scene: 他需要做膝盖手术。He needs surgery on his knee.
sceneCN: 这里 surgery 是「外科手术」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他需要做膝盖手术。

senses.title: Medical operation
senses.definition: treatment by cutting into the body
senses.definitionCN: 通过切开身体进行的治疗
senses.example: He needs surgery on his knee.
senses.exampleCN: 他需要做膝盖手术。
senses.why: This is the main medical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的医学义项。

senses.title: A doctor's office
senses.definition: a place where a doctor sees patients, in British use
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中医生看诊的地方
senses.example: The surgery opens at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所九点开门。
senses.why: This is a British place sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是英式的地点义项。

senses.title: The branch of medicine
senses.definition: the field of medicine that uses operations
senses.definitionCN: 以手术为手段的医学分支
senses.example: She teaches surgery at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学教外科。
senses.why: Here the word names a discipline.
senses.whyCN: 这里指一门学科。

intro.en: Surgery comes from Greek cheirourgia, hand work.
intro.cn: surgery 来自希腊语 cheirourgia，意为手工操作。

items.en: Cheir meant hand.
Ergon meant work.
Cheirourgia meant hand work, especially healing.
items.cn: cheirourgia 意为手工操作，尤指治疗。

items.en: Chirurgia meant surgery.
Surgerie meant surgery.
Surgery named operations and clinics.

note.en: Surgery is compared with look-alike words and with words for medical treatment.
note.cn: 把 surgery 与形近词以及表示医疗的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Surgery is healing done with careful hands.
normalIntro.cn: surgery 是用一双谨慎的手完成的治疗。

normal.en: He needs surgery on his knee.
normal.cn: 他需要做膝盖手术。

normal.en: She had heart surgery last year.
normal.cn: 她去年做了心脏手术。

normal.en: The surgery opens at nine.
normal.cn: 诊所九点开门。

normal.en: He is recovering from surgery.
normal.cn: 他正在术后恢复。

normal.en: Plastic surgery is common in some cities.
normal.cn: 整形手术在一些城市很常见。

abstract.en: Surgery is trust placed in steady hands.
abstract.cn: 手术，是把信任交给一双稳当的手。

abstract.en: The body can be repaired and also remembers.
abstract.cn: 身体可以被修复，也会记得。

abstract.en: Healing begins before the wound closes.
abstract.cn: 愈合，在伤口合上之前就开始了。

examples.en: He needs surgery on his knee.
examples.cn: 他需要做膝盖手术。

examples.en: She had heart surgery last year.
examples.cn: 她去年做了心脏手术。

examples.en: He is recovering from surgery.
examples.cn: 他正在术后恢复。

dict_mnemonic.text: surgery 是「外科手术」，英式英语中也可指「诊所」；surgeon 是外科医生，surgical 是外科的。

root: 来自希腊语 cheirourgia（手工操作），由 cheir（手）与 ergon（工作）组成，经拉丁语与古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Surgery means a medical operation, a doctor's office in British use, or the field of operative medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: surgery 表示外科手术、英式英语中的诊所，或外科这一学科。

core.en: Healing through careful handwork.
core.cn: 通过谨慎的手工操作来治疗。

branches.en: He needs surgery on his knee.
branches.cn: 他需要做膝盖手术。

branches.en: She had heart surgery last year.
branches.cn: 她去年做了心脏手术。

branches.en: The surgery opens at nine.
branches.cn: 诊所九点开门。

branches.en: She teaches surgery at the university.
branches.cn: 她在大学教外科。

branches.en: An operation and a discipline share one name.
branches.cn: 手术与学科共用一个名字。

intro.en: Surgery builds surgeon, surgical, and surgically.
intro.cn: surgery 可构成 surgeon、surgical 和 surgically。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek cheirourgia, hand work.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是希腊语 cheirourgia，意为手工操作。

items.exampleCN: 两名外科医生加入了团队。

latinEntries.example: Cheir is the first element of surgery.

latinEntries.example: Ergon also gave English energy.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ergon 也演变为英语的 energy。

latinEntries.example: Chirurgia led to French surgerie.
latinEntries.exampleCN: chirurgia 演变为法语 surgerie。

definition_en: to go beyond a limit, record or standard, or to be better than someone or something else
core_image: 终点线旁的数字牌被人越过，上一年的纪录还挂在牌上，新数字已经翻过去
scene: 年底还没到，出口额就已经比去年全年更多。Exports are expected to surpass last year's total.
sceneCN: 这里指在数量上超过原有水平（第 1 个义项：数量或数字超过）；句意为出口额预计会超过去年全年总量。图中可辨识物件：终点线、翻过去的数字牌、旧纪录。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「非凡的；超越的」
由否定前缀加已然词构成，义为「无可匹敌的」
由该动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可超越的」（少用）
由该动词加已然词尾构成，义为「已被超越的」

senses.title: To exceed a number
senses.definition: to be greater than a stated figure, total or level
senses.definitionCN: 大于某个给定的数字、总量或水平
senses.example: Sales surpassed ten million units this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年销量超过了一千万台。
senses.why: The Old French verb meant to pass over, and a figure is something you can pass.
senses.whyCN: 古法语动词意为「越过」，而数字正是可以越过去的东西。

senses.title: To outperform a rival
senses.definition: to do better than a competitor in a contest or market
senses.definitionCN: 在竞赛或市场中表现得比对手更好
senses.example: The small team surpassed three larger firms in the trial.
senses.exampleCN: 这支小团队在测试中胜过了三家更大的公司。
senses.why: A race is the original scene: one runner passes another and is now ahead.
senses.whyCN: 赛跑是最初的场景：一名跑者越过另一名，就跑到前面了。

senses.title: To exceed expectations
senses.definition: to be better or larger than people had predicted
senses.definitionCN: 比人们此前预料的更好或更大
senses.example: The response to the appeal surpassed every forecast.
senses.exampleCN: 这次呼吁得到的响应超出了所有预测。
senses.why: Expectations set a line in advance, and surpassing is crossing that line.
senses.whyCN: 预期提前画了一条线，超过就是越过那条线。

senses.title: To break a record
senses.definition: to go beyond the best result previously achieved
senses.definitionCN: 超过此前取得的最好成绩
senses.example: She surpassed the national record by two hundredths of a second.
senses.exampleCN: 她以百分之二秒打破了全国纪录。
senses.why: A record is the highest mark on the board, and the verb names the moment it falls.
senses.whyCN: 纪录是板上最高的刻度，这个词命名它被刷下的那一刻。

senses.title: To go beyond a limit of ability
senses.definition: to be more than a person or system can reach or handle
senses.definitionCN: 超过人或系统所能达到或处理的范围
senses.example: The noise surpassed the level the equipment could measure.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声超过了设备能够测量的水平。
senses.why: A limit is a wall, and surpassing passes over it rather than around it.
senses.whyCN: 极限是一堵墙，而超过是从上方越过去，不是绕过去。

senses.title: To be superior in quality
senses.definition: to be of better quality than another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类的另一事物之上
senses.example: The finish surpassed every sample we had tested.
senses.exampleCN: 这层表面处理胜过我们测过的所有样品。
senses.why: Quality can be ranked, and the higher rank simply sits beyond the lower one.
senses.whyCN: 质量可以排位，较高的位次就落在较低位次之外。

senses.title: To outdo one's earlier self
senses.definition: to do better than one's own previous performance
senses.definitionCN: 比自己以往的表现做得更好
senses.example: He surpassed his own best time in the final heat.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一组超过了自己的最好成绩。
senses.why: The rival can be oneself, which is why the word often appears with the reflexive form.
senses.whyCN: 对手可以就是自己，所以这个词常与反身形式同现。

senses.title: To go over a set ceiling
senses.definition: to rise above a ceiling set by policy, safety or design
senses.definitionCN: 上升到由政策、安全或设计设定的上限之上
senses.example: Demand surpassed the capacity of the old substation.
senses.exampleCN: 需求超过了旧变电站的容量。
senses.why: Every design has a ceiling, and surpassing it is the point where a plan stops being safe.
senses.whyCN: 每个设计都有上限，超过它就是方案不再安全的那个点。

intro.en: Surpass comes from Old French surpasser, to go beyond, from sur-, over, and passer, to pass, which goes back to Latin passus, a step. English adopted it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 surpasser「越过」，由 sur-「在上、超过」与 passer「经过」构成，而 passer 可追溯到拉丁语 passus「一步」；英语十六世纪引入。

items.en: Passus meant a step or a pace, and it is the source of pass, passage and surpass alike.
items.cn: 这个词意为一步或一步的距离，是 pass、passage、surpass 共同的来源。

items.en: The prefix behind sur- meant above or over, and it survives in super, supreme and surface.
items.cn: sur- 背后的前缀意为在上、越过，仍见于 super、supreme、surface。

items.en: The French verb meant to go beyond or to exceed, and it was used of limits, rivals and expectations.
items.cn: 这个法语动词意为越过、超过，用于界限、对手与预期。

items.en: English adopted the verb in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain and is usually given only as that century.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪采用这个动词，确切首见年代不确定，通常只给「十六世纪」。

items.en: Surplus, survive and surrender share the same over- prefix with different roots behind it.
items.cn: surplus、survive、surrender 共享同一「在上」前缀，背后的词根各不相同。

items.en: Sport gave the verb its fixed objects record and rival, which keep the race image alive.
items.cn: 体育给这个动词添了纪录与对手这两个固定宾语，让赛跑画面延续至今。

note.en: The first group shares the pass root or looks close; the second group names neighbouring ideas of excelling.
note.cn: 第一组与「surpass」共享 pass 词根或只是形近；第二组是与「胜过」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning exceptional, literally going beyond others.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指非凡的，字面是「越过他人」。

entries.definition: Not exceeded by anything, the negative adjective of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指无人超过的，是这个动词的否定形容词。

entries.definition: Capable of being exceeded, a rare but regular form.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被超过的，少用但构词规则。

entries.definition: To go by or beyond, the base verb inside surpass.
entries.definitionCN: 指经过或越过，是这个词内部的基础动词。

entries.definition: An amount over what is needed; the prefix matches but the root is to be more.
entries.definitionCN: 指超出所需的数量；前缀相同，词根是「更多」。

entries.definition: The top layer, from sur- and face; the prefix matches, the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指表层，由「在上」前缀与「面」构成；前缀相同，词根不同。

entries.definition: To go beyond a number or a limit, the neutral technical verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指超出数量或限度，是中性技术说法。

entries.definition: To do better than someone in the same activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指在同一活动中做得比某人更好。

entries.definition: To perform better than a rival, common in business.
entries.definitionCN: 指表现优于对手，商务常用。

entries.definition: To defeat or do better than, in plain speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指击败或胜过，口语说法。

entries.definition: To go beyond a category or limit altogether, often in a philosophical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体上超越某个范畴或限度，常带哲学意味。

entries.definition: To be higher than a previous figure, used of charts and lists.
entries.definitionCN: 指高于先前数字，多用于榜单。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the step root, the over prefix, and the sporting phrases that keep the race image alive.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「一步」词根、「在上」前缀，以及让赛跑画面延续的体育搭配。

normal.en: Passus is a step, and surpass is to step over the line that was there.
normal.cn: passus 是「一步」，而这个词就是跨过原先那条线。

normal.en: Sur- means over, the same prefix seen in surplus and surface.
normal.cn: sur- 意为「在上」，与 surplus、surface 同一前缀。

normal.en: Athletes surpass a record; firms surpass expectations and rivals.
normal.cn: 运动员打破纪录，企业超出预期、胜过对手。

normal.en: Unsurpassed is the negative adjective: nobody has gone past it.
normal.cn: 「无可匹敌的」是否定形容词：没人越过去过。

normal.en: Unlike transcend, surpass is measurable: a number, a time or a rank moves past another.
normal.cn: 与 transcend 不同，surpass 是可测量的：数字、时间或名次越到另一个前面。

abstract.en: To surpass is to make yesterday's ceiling today's floor.
abstract.cn: 超越，就是把昨天的天花板变成今天的地板。

abstract.en: Every record is only a place where someone stopped being measured.
abstract.cn: 每一项纪录都只是有人停止被测量的那个位置。

abstract.en: Transcend changes the scale; surpass merely moves along it, and knowing which one you need is the real skill.
abstract.cn: 超越范畴是换一把尺，胜过只是在同一把尺上往前挪，分得清两者才是真本事。

examples.en: Demand for the service surpassed all earlier estimates.
examples.cn: 这项服务的需求超出了此前所有估计。

examples.en: Her second novel surpassed the first in every review.
examples.cn: 她的第二部小说在每一篇评论中都胜过了第一部。

examples.en: The river surpassed its danger level after two days of rain.
examples.cn: 两天降雨之后，这条河超过了警戒水位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑟帕斯」——终点牌被翻过去，旧纪录留在上面：超过、胜过

root: 拉丁语 passus「一步」→ 古法语 surpasser「越过」（sur-「在上」+ passer「经过」）；英语十六世纪引入。与 transcend 不同，本词强调可测量的越线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all cross a line: a number, a rival, a forecast, a record, a limit, a quality, one's own best and a ceiling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在越过一条线：数字、对手、预测、纪录、极限、质量、自己的最好成绩与上限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner crosses the line and the board turns past last year's figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑者冲过终点线，数字牌翻过去年的数字。

branches.en: THE FIGURE IS PASSED: a total or a ceiling is left below the new reading.
branches.cn: 数字被越过：总量或上限被留在新读数之下。

branches.en: THE RIVAL IS BEHIND: a competitor or a sample now ranks lower.
branches.cn: 对手落到后面：竞争者或样品的名次更低。

branches.en: THE FORECAST IS BEATEN: what people expected turns out to be too small.
branches.cn: 预测被打破：人们预想的原来偏小。

branches.en: THE MARK FALLS: a record or one's own previous best is replaced.
branches.cn: 刻度被刷下：纪录或自己从前的最好成绩被取代。

branches.en: THE ABILITY IS OUTRUN: a limit of reach, handling or understanding is passed.
branches.cn: 能力被跑过：触及、处理或理解的极限被越过。

intro.en: Surpass joins an over-prefix to a verb of stepping, and both pieces are Latin in origin though the compound is French.
intro.cn: 这个词把「在上」的前缀接到表示「迈步」的动词上，两部分都源自拉丁语，但复合发生在法语。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies passus and super; the French compound surpasser then supplied English, and every piece is well recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了 passus 与 super；法语复合词 surpasser 再提供英语，每个部件都有清楚记录。

items.example: The noun is the source of pass and surpass.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 pass 与 surpass 的来源。

items.example: The French verb supplied the moving half.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词提供「移动」的那一半。

items.example: It marks the line being crossed.
items.exampleCN: 它标出被越过的那条线。

items.example: The Latin form behind the French prefix.
items.exampleCN: 法语前缀背后的拉丁形式。

items.example: The compound entered English almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词几乎原样进入英语。

items.meaning: in the course of, or to a high degree

由否定前缀加已然词构成，义为「无可匹敌的」
由该动词加「可……的」形容词尾构成，义为「可超越的」（少用）

definition_en: an amount left over after what is needed has been used
core_image: 仓库里堆着多出来的粮食袋，标签写着剩余
scene: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
sceneCN: 这里 surplus 是「剩余」（第 1 个义项）；句意：今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。

senses.title: An amount left over
senses.definition: an amount that remains after needs are met
senses.definitionCN: 满足需求后剩下的数量
senses.example: This year's harvest left a surplus that could be sold to the next village.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的收成有剩余，可以卖给邻村。
senses.why: This is the basic sense of something left over.
senses.whyCN: 这是「剩下之物」的基本义项。

senses.title: A financial gain
senses.definition: the amount by which income is greater than spending
senses.definitionCN: 收入大于支出的部分

latinIntro.en: The Latin vivere, to live, also appears in revive and vivid.

latinEntries.example: Vivere is the living root of survival.

definition_zh: 幸存；幸免于；存活；比…活得长
definition_en: to continue to live after danger, or to live longer than someone
core_image: 风暴过后，一株小树仍立在断枝之间
scene: 只有少数植物能在沙漠中存活。Only a few plants can survive in the desert.
sceneCN: 这里 survive 是「存活」（第 1 个义项）；句意：只有少数植物能在沙漠中存活。

senses.title: To stay alive
senses.definition: to continue to live, especially in difficult conditions
senses.definitionCN: 尤其在困境中继续活着
senses.example: Only a few plants can survive in the desert.
senses.exampleCN: 只有少数植物能在沙漠中存活。
senses.why: This is the core sense of staying alive.
senses.whyCN: 这是「活下来」的核心义项。

senses.title: To live through danger
senses.definition: to continue to live after an accident or attack
senses.definitionCN: 在事故或攻击之后仍然活着
senses.example: She survived the accident without serious injury.
senses.exampleCN: 她在事故中幸存，没有受重伤。
senses.why: Here the word focuses on passing through danger.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调闯过危险。

senses.title: To outlive someone
senses.definition: to continue to live after another person has died
senses.definitionCN: 在他人去世后仍然活着
senses.example: He survived his wife by ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他比妻子多活了十年。
senses.why: This sense compares two lives.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项比较两条生命。

intro.en: Survive is built from Latin for living beyond.
intro.cn: survive 由拉丁语中表示「活过」的部分构成。

items.en: Super meant beyond.
Vivere meant to live.
Survivre meant to outlive.
Survive meant to remain alive.
Survive extended to enduring hardship.

note.en: Survive is compared with look-alike words and with verbs for lasting.
note.cn: 把 survive 与形近词以及表示持续存在的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Survive means to keep living past danger or another life.
normalIntro.cn: survive 意为活过危险，或活得比他人更久。

normal.cn: 只有少数植物能在沙漠中存活。

normal.cn: 她在事故中幸存，没有受重伤。

normal.en: He survived his wife by ten years.

normal.en: They survived on berries and rain water.
normal.cn: 他们靠浆果和雨水生存。

normal.en: The business survived the hard winter.
normal.cn: 这家企业在艰难的冬天挺了过来。

abstract.en: To survive is to carry life through a test.
abstract.cn: 幸存就是带着生命穿过一场考验。

abstract.en: The word joins living with going beyond.
abstract.cn: 这个词把「活着」与「越过」结合起来。

abstract.en: What survives is not unchanged; it is what could bend.
abstract.cn: 幸存下来的并非一成不变，而是能弯曲的东西。
